title: New Year, Fresh Cut: Booking Your First Haircut of the Year
hero_alt: Fireworks bursting over a city skyline at night
card_text: Trying something new for the new year? How to plan the change, how holiday week falls, and when the holiday fee applies.
lede: If you want your first haircut of the new year, book it now. The week between Christmas and New Year's is short at my shop: Wednesday is closed as always, and the holiday itself carries a {{holiday_fee}} fee on top of the service. The regular days around it are regular price, so a slot on one of those starts the year at the usual cost.
Here's how the calendar falls, how to plan a new style, and what to book.

blocks.heading: How the days fall.
blocks.lead: New Year's Day lands on a Friday this time.
rows: Open regular hours, holiday fee applies
paragraphs: I'm open on holidays at my regular hours for that day of the week. The {{holiday_fee}} fee applies only on the holiday itself, not on the days before or after it.

blocks.heading: Change it on purpose.
blocks.lead: Start the year with a plan.
paragraphs: A new year is a natural time to try the cut you've been saving photos of. The trick is knowing what your hair can do right now. Going shorter can happen in one visit. Going longer takes months of growing, and a cut that shapes the in-between stages.
Bring a photo of the style and a photo of your hair as it is today, or text both to me before you book. That tells us whether it's a one-appointment change or the first step of a few.
If you want a big change but you're nervous about it, try it in stages. Take the sides shorter first, live with it, and adjust the top next time.

blocks.heading: A cut you'll keep up.
blocks.lead: Pick one that fits your mornings.
paragraphs: The new style only works if you can wear it on a regular Tuesday. Ask yourself how long you'll spend on it before work, whether a hat is part of your day, and how sharp you want it to stay.

A textured crop like the one in the photo above is a low-effort place to start: short sides, a choppy top pushed forward, and very little to do once it's dry. A skin fade or a hard part asks for more frequent visits to stay crisp.
Once you've picked, book the next appointment while you're thinking about it. Booksy shows open times ahead, and the week only has so many of them.

items.title: Signature Cut
items.body: Adds a beard trim or line-up, a hot towel and razor detailing, for a new year that includes the beard.

items.title: Luxury Grooming Experience
items.body: A consultation first, then the cut, a beard sculpt, a wash, steam, hot towels, waxing, a basic design and a fragrance finish. The full reset.

blocks.heading: Plan around the break.
paragraphs: Heading out of town for the holidays? Book the cut for the days before you leave, or for the first open slot after you get back, so you aren't hunting for a time in the middle of the trip.

Grew a beard over the break? Bring it in rather than shaving it off at home. The Signature Cut can trim it down or line it up, and the Straight Razor Beard Shave ({{price:straight-razor-beard-shave}}, {{minutes:straight-razor-beard-shave}}) takes it off completely with hot towels.
Holiday plans change fast. If yours do, move or cancel the appointment in Booksy right away, since a no-show or a late cancellation may be charged a fee, and someone else may want that slot.

items.q: Are you open on New Year's Day?
items.a: Yes. I'm open my regular Friday hours, and appointments on the holiday itself carry a {{holiday_fee}} holiday fee.

items.q: Is there a holiday fee the rest of the week?
items.a: No. The fee applies only on the holiday itself. The days around it are regular prices.

items.q: Are you open on Wednesday, December 30?
items.a: No. The shop is closed every Wednesday and every Sunday, holiday week included.
